summary: release moves builds through release channels: it keeps an lkgr (last known good) pointer and channel pointers such as canary, each naming a commit and an artifact digest. It exists so that what ships is always a build that passed its checks, with every move recorded and reversible.

how_it_works.title: lkgr
how_it_works.text: lkgr is the newest main commit whose required post-submit builders are all green, using the gardener's definitions. A pending, missing or cancelled result is not green, so a missing signal holds lkgr in place; the workflow recomputes it every 10 minutes.

how_it_works.title: The release executor
how_it_works.text: Only the executor moves lkgr and channel pointers. Each move is an operation whose key is committed to the release-state branch before anything else changes, so a retry with the same intent does nothing twice.

how_it_works.title: Channels and rollback
how_it_works.text: A channel pointer names a commit and an artifact digest; canary is promoted from lkgr, and dev would take canary's. Rollback points the channel at the newest earlier value from its history without rebuilding, and after every move a channels.json manifest is written for the installer.

how_it_works.title: The daily canary
how_it_works.text: Once a day the canary workflow takes lkgr's commit, builds it, runs the full tests, runs property tests again as a fuzz smoke, deploys and probes it, and only then promotes it. The first failing stage holds that commit and keeps the previous canary, A watchdog is meant to restart a run GitHub drops, but it uses the same throttled scheduler; on 5 October the dropped run was started by hand, and a daily backstop is planned.

how_it_works.title: Daily report
how_it_works.text: After each day's canary a report job files one issue saying what shipped, what was held and why, and what canary names now. The same text is kept on release-state.

status.text: lkgr, channel pointers with rollback, the daily canary and its report are all merged. In v0 only canary can be promoted: dev and stable are declared, but a channel that needs an approval, a soak or health signals is refused.

The first canary ran on 5 October, started by hand because GitHub skipped the 06:17 schedule. Both repos passed every stage, nothing was held, and canary moved on release-state; the report is issue 15. GitHub runs this repo's schedules far less often than written (lkgr ran 4 times between 17:48 and 02:25 UTC, then not again before 07:00), and canary-watchdog uses the same scheduler. A daily backstop is planned.
A day when lkgr has not moved, or its commit was held before, leaves a recorded no-op instead of a new canary.

The release executor's identity does not exist yet, so target-repo ref writes are skipped and recorded as such, while the pointer still moves on release-state. That branch is only as safe as push access to this repo until a ruleset protects it.
Soak, automatic rollback, a real fuzz stage and the dev channel are out of scope for v0 and planned for v1; stable and staged rollout are planned for v2.
